summary: For bacteria and archaea, structured shape and growth-condition records exist: BacDive strain records (API reachable, Morphology section present but empty in the three strains sampled) and the Madin et al. trait synthesis (14 phenotypic traits for ~170,000 strain and ~15,000 species records, figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4843290.v3), though whether cell shape is among its traits was not read. No comparable shape inventory was found for protozoa or other eukaryotic minute cells, and no dataset records the same organism's shape across physical conditions; AlgaeBase and the Cell Image Library expose no queryable structured data.
next_step: Download condensed_traits_NCBI (figshare 13557827) to confirm cell-shape and cell-size columns and count the distinct shape classes; find or compile a protist shape/size table (e.g. from PR2 or a ciliate trait database) and define the macro-organism contrast group before pre-registering a morphospace-breadth test.
obstacles_confirmed: Protozoa are poorly represented next to bacteria: every structured shape source found is prokaryotic.
Shape fields are coarse categories: BacDive/trait syntheses store shape as a class, so 'limited range' will depend on the coding scheme.
No dataset records shape of the same taxon under varying temperature or osmotic conditions.
